title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Procedural Matters Related to Civil Cases Involving Foreign State Immunity
keywords_en: jurisdiction; intellectual property; civil cases involving foreign state immunity
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Procedural Matters in Civil Cases Involving Foreign State Immunity

Fa [2025] No. 39

Higher People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

For the purposes of properly adjudicating civil cases involving foreign state immunity, protecting the lawful rights and interests of the parties, and upholding the sovereign equality of states, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Foreign State Immunity Law of the People's Republic of China and the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the following matters are hereby notified:

1. A foreign state and its property enjoy immunity from jurisdiction in the courts of China, except as otherwise provided by the Foreign State Immunity Law. In respect of an action filed against a foreign state as defined in Article 2 of the Foreign State Immunity Law as the defendant or a third party, the people's court shall examine whether the statement of claim specifies the existence of an exception to immunity provided for in the Foreign State Immunity Law. If the statement of claim does not so specify, the people's court shall provide clarification to the plaintiff. If, after clarification, the plaintiff still fails to make such specification, the people's court shall not accept the case.

2. First-instance civil cases in which a foreign state as defined in Article 2 of the Foreign State Immunity Law is the defendant or a third party shall be under the jurisdiction of the intermediate people's court located in the seat of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government that has jurisdiction over foreign-related civil and commercial cases (see the annex for details), as well as the maritime court, financial court, and intellectual property court.

A people's court other than those specified in the preceding paragraph shall not accept an action against a foreign state as the defendant or a third party; if it has already accepted such an action, it shall render a ruling transferring the case to a people's court that has jurisdiction.

3. When serving a summons or other litigation documents on a foreign state, a people's court shall effect service in the manner provided for in an international treaty concluded or jointly acceded to by that foreign state and China, or in another manner that is accepted by that foreign state and not prohibited by Chinese law. There is no requirement for a sequential order of application between the two manners of service mentioned above.

If service cannot be completed through either of the two manners of service mentioned above, the Supreme People's Court may effect service through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs by means of a diplomatic note.

If service is effected by means of a diplomatic note as provided for in the preceding paragraph, the people's court shall report the summons or other litigation documents to be served level by level to the Supreme People's Court.

When serving a summons or other litigation documents on a foreign state, a people's court shall not effect service by public announcement.

4. When serving a summons or other litigation documents on a foreign state, a people's court shall, in accordance with the provisions of an international treaty concluded or jointly acceded to by that foreign state and China, attach a translation in the relevant language; in the absence of any such international treaty, the people's court shall attach a translation in the official language of that foreign state.

When serving a copy of the statement of claim on a foreign state, the people's court shall also serve litigation documents such as a notice of response and a notice of evidence submission, notifying the foreign state to submit a statement of defense within three months after receiving the copy of the statement of claim. If the foreign state applies for an extension of the time for submitting its defense, the people's court shall examine the application and decide whether to grant it.

5. If a foreign state raises an objection to jurisdiction on the ground that it enjoys immunity from jurisdiction within the time limit for submitting its defense, the people's court shall conduct a comprehensive examination, in accordance with the Foreign State Immunity Law, of whether the foreign state enjoys immunity from jurisdiction, and may, depending on the circumstances, hear the opinions of the parties.

If a foreign state only presents its opinions for the purpose of participating in the procedure for examining the objection to jurisdiction, this shall not be deemed as acceptance of the jurisdiction of the people's court.

6. If a foreign state neither raises an objection to jurisdiction on the ground that it enjoys immunity from jurisdiction within the time limit for submitting its defense, nor appears in court to participate in the proceedings, the people's court shall, ex officio, proactively examine whether the foreign state enjoys immunity from jurisdiction, and may, depending on the circumstances, hear the opinions of the parties.

7. Where, in the course of handling civil cases involving foreign state immunity, a people's court needs the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to issue a certificate regarding factual issues of an act of state, the people's court shall, in accordance with Article 19 of the Foreign State Immunity Law, report level by level to the Supreme People's Court, which shall then consult the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to request the issuance of such a certificate.

8. Where, in the course of hearing a case, a foreign state becomes a defendant or a third party because it has been added as a party, by counterclaim, or otherwise, the matter shall be handled in accordance with this Notice.

Problems encountered during the implementation of this Notice shall be promptly reported to the Supreme People's Court.
